item.title: Gap semester
item.description: For various reasons, the latter half of my 2025 ended up becoming a gap semester. I graduated undergrad back in May with no certain future prospect of the upcoming years: I didn’t hear back anything promising from my PhD admissions cycle nor job applications. Fortunately I had an internship lined up for the summer, and there I made connections to then lead to my current work with Purdue. Herein, I spent a good amount of my time from August to now leading a research project and learning a lot. I then got into MS starting spring 2026 and decided to commit to grad school. So looking back, my fall 2025 now looks like a gap semester.

item.title: 4 signs a ramen shop might not be great before you enter it (in America)
item.description: Good and great ramen isn’t difficult to find in Japan. So, how come most ramen I come across in America don’t hit the same spot? I have no expertise in explaining the history behind how ramen was brought to the United States and how its cultural dominance exploded (think instant ramen and college students, or saimin). What I can say are a few tricks that I’ve uncovered in determining if a ramen shop may not be so great, even before you ever enter it and order food. To preface, this is based off my experience eating ramen in NYC, Boston, and LA. These tricks may not apply to places that exist outside of these three cities, but I hope it helps the reader get a better sense of what good ramen is like.

item.title: On Taking Notes
item.description: I’ve always felt like the way I took notes is very sub-optimal. Whether it was for class, meetings, or self-study, the way I took notes seemed flawed compared to how others did. I think seeing people color-code or create a bajillion nested folders has made me self-aware of my messyness and possibly insecure of it; I thus sought out to improve my note-taking skills. After years of improvements, upgrades, and optimizations, I realized that, drumroll, the way I took notes originally was near-optimal and better than the rest for my needs. Here I’ll cover each and my thoughts regarding its pros/cons, and why I eventually just went full circle to my original note-taking practices.

item.title: Yapping and White papers
item.description: I’ve often been called out for yapping, been called a yapper, or been told I speak yapanese - these are synonymous with the idea that I can’t shut up. From this, I’ve caught myself talking for prolong periods of time, possibly making a roundabout argument / case that isn’t clear cut and thus misleading. To work on this, I wanted to take inspiration from Nash’s thesis, known to be the one of the most short but influential pieces of writing ever, and learn how to present myself with more clarity and conciseness. As such, I wanted to read other works that get the point across in an efficient manner.

item.title: Ai/Robots in Fiction ver. 8 -- Metal Gear Solid 2
item.description: The Metal Gear Solid series is a cult favorite for many reasons, but to give a sentence to sell you on the series, it’s an over-the-top serious anti-war story with tons of goofy boss fights and funny characters. While there’s tons of comedy and fun gameplay, the overall messages found within the games is profound and to me, I think Metal Gear Solid 2 is where its significance kickstarts. I’d like to explain the brilliance of this specific piece here.

item.title: Ai/Robots in Fiction ver. 7 -- CRYMACHINA
item.description:
Preface

I was in Japan during the winter break, visiting family like usual. I tend to go to BookOff to buy used goods (thrifting clothes mostly) and was in the game section when a certain piece caught my eye. The game’s package had beautiful art with its composition - surely it’s a well-known game I thought. To my surprise, this game isn’t very known and has a relatively low Metacritic score (I literally don’t trust any of these dog-ass video game critics especially IGN) and meh user ratings (I trust these reviews though). So, I just put it back in the aisle and went with my day.

item.title: Ai/Robots in Fiction ver. 6 -- Summer Wars
item.description:
To my former labmate and friend Yohei Hayamizu, Summer Wars was one of the more influential works that sparked his decision to enter robotics, AI, and in general, higher technology. And for 6-year-old me when I first watched it, I could not agree more. The breathtaking music, animation, and crazy breadth in terms of technology is just Hyminal to any tech junkie.

Summer Wars Poster

Summer Wars is at its core, a story that revolves around the setting of future Japan, and the integration of Oz, a digital world akin to a metaverse, in Japanese society. Oz is heavily engrained within every aspect of society - from mainly acting as a social media hub to a control unit for various physical “computerized” entities like fire hydrants and traffic signals (we’ll get back to this second point later). Everyone has their own customized characters that represent their identities, and Oz acts as a second society for people. Users can participate in various events, transactions, and games within this digital world, e.g., one of the protagonist’s allies, alias King Kazuma, is famous in Oz for being the number one hand-to-hand combat fighter.

item.title: Ai/Robots in Fiction ver. 5 -- 13 Sentinels
item.description:
“Get in the robot, Shinji” - Misato, Neon Genesis Evangelion

This famous quote encompasses the unwillingness by Shinji to pilot the 01 Eva due to interpersonal depression and external expectations and duty set from society. Now, imagine this, but add 12 more characters who bare the responsibility to pilot mechs to protect humanity. This is the setup for the game 13 Sentinels: Aegis Rim developed by Vanillaware and released by Atlas. I already love Atlas (notably the Persona Games, Metaphor, and Catherine), so as I looked for other serious games to play on my switch, I stumbled upon this. And boy oh boy, this game is batshit insane.

item.title: Ai/Robots in Fiction ver. 4 -- Doraemon and Dead Dead Demon's Dededededestruction
item.description:
With the anime released, I thought it’d be great for me to introduce Dead Dead Demon’s Dededededestruction (DDDD) next. This is a manga made by esteemed author Inio Asano, famous for Solanin and his masterpiece, Oyasumi Punpun. This work is not as depressing as his other works (which is, in some sense, a good thing), but still conveys a great depth of existential dread so I’d highly recommend reading it.

DDDD

item.title: Ai/Robots in Fiction ver. 3 -- Ai: The Somnium Files
item.description:
AI: The Somnium Files is a murder mystery game created by Kotaro Uchikoshi, known for the Zero Escape series (AMAZING STUFF). You play as Date, an amnesiac detective and aim to solve a potential revived serial killing in a futuristic society. While I can definitely talk all day about the entire plot and twists that happen throughout the game, I’ll just stick to the AI stuff.

The entire core of AI in this game follows a single character, but before we get into that, I first want to give a little background, specifically, the title of the game.

item.title: Ai/Robots in Fiction ver. 2 -- Pluto
item.description:
Pluto follows a futuristic world in which technology is much advanced, to the point where robots exist in our every day lives. While this shows a great promise for science, Pluto also posits an important question: “What happens if robots gain consciousness?” Can humans and robots coexist in such a world, or will this feat cause one of the factions to drive the other into extinction?

Pluto Volume 7 Cover.

item.title: Ai/Robots in Fiction ver. 1 -- NieR
item.description:
I like entertainment, and a huge part of the reason I’m into math and cs and stuff is due to the fiction material I’ve ingested. Subsequently, I want to talk about all the fiction material that’s impacted my life and my thoughts.

This is because sci-fi brings up many points that ponder how the world will be impacted by new technology. I mean for one, War Games hypothesized how a hacker could breach the military and launch a nuke - this fictional story persuaded the federal government to relook at the, then current, regulations regarding internet protocol.

item.title: Undergraduate research, through university and REUs
item.description:
Update (Aug 16, 2025): Some of the context of this post has been modified b/c I lost the relevant data awhile back and had not reuploaded this post until today. Nevertheless, a decent chunk of this post is still relevant, so I hope it is of use to the reader.

Within the past year, I gained various life experiences, though one of the more non-private ones I’m comfortable sharing to strangers on the internet (besides my Goodreads book list!) is my undergraduate research experience. This book is god-tier.

item.title: Burari - Chicken Paitan Classic
item.description:
• Price: ¥990
  • Rating: 9/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-18
  • Review: The soup is the star of the dish - crazily gelatinous and really clings to the noodles and your palate, but not to the point of being overbearing. Chashu, celery, scallions, egg, and the red pepper add a nice burst of flavor and appeal.

item.title: Charume - Chuuka Soba w/ Wontons
item.description:
• Price: ¥1200
  • Rating: 8.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-01-08
  • Review: classic bowl with seafood broth and a soy sauce base. everything is really clean and refreshing, and the wontons add a fresh twist. for me, the star is the chicken chashu which has a clean fattyness w/ a slight spice aftertaste that shines through the rest of the bowl. overall, a great classic example of chuuka soba w/ a seafood broth.

item.title: Downtown - Mushroom Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $15
  • Rating: 5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-04-01
  • Review: overall just tastes like shin ramyun, idk how else to describe it. This was a vegan option at an american restaurant so I was like “why not.” The noodles were decent, but the soup is a mushroom base that only reminds me of shin. It’s pretty sad as a ramen, and even more so as a vegan option. I pity vegetarians/vegans who get served this. Overall the toppings don’t make sense either, though the mushrooms were nice. I like shin, don’t get me wrong. But I only like it as an instant ramen option, not as a “go outside to try food at a restaurant” type of ramen. It’s the only ramen so far which I didn’t finish and made my friend eat instead. I mean, I had low expectations and it met my low bar.

item.title: Edomondo - Jiro-style Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥950
  • Rating: 7.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-21
  • Review: (for the price, you can get small/med/large portion of noods for and i accidentally got a large which now I’m in a food coma) the broth is a bit salty but b/c you can get a buttload of toppings for free (bean sprouts, cabbage, raw garlic), it easily cuts thru w/ the thick noodles. theres a quail egg and a really tender chashu. the amount adds up to probs like 2000 calories or smth but flavorwise its really heavy. its a nice little shop tho, tons of retro video game motifs. i was eating while listening to final fantasy music and looking at ryu and slime on a sign.

item.title: Hatori - Ginger Shoyu Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥950
  • Rating: 9/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-17
  • Review: Clean shoyu soup base with a sharp ginger topping accent. The chashu pork is melt-in-your-mouth tender and the other toppings were executed well. For the price, 9/10.

item.title: hidden content
item.description:
congrats for finding this, albeit it’s not very hidden since all you do is add posts/hidden. Anyway, here I write some other stuff.

🇯🇵 Japan suggestions

Everybody and their mama going to Japan these past years (2023 onwards) so I’ve gotten asked for suggestions. Here I just type some out:

  • ramen: kikanbo for a spicy miso, kyushu jangara for tonkotsu
  • jpn fast food: yoshinoya/sukiya for beef bowls (either called gyu-meshi or gyu-don); coco-ichibanya for jpn curry
  • chain restaurants: tori kizoku for chicken skewers; gyukaku for jpn bbq (but theres gyukaku in flushing so u can always try that back there); gyoza no ohsho for chinese-jpn food; u can always find pasta/okonomiyaki/other food chain stores near the top floor of malls/department stores
  • korean food: any store in shin-ookubo bc thats basically ktown, i went here (https://maps.app.goo.gl/pWhTTmXz45eM8oF16?g_st=ipc) before I think and found it pretty good
  • desserts: the cream puffs at cow cow kitchen (there’s a location next to akihabara station); the pudding from morozoff’s (jpn pudding is more like flan and not the thing jello makes lol); pon de ring from mister donuts
  • places1: yanaka ginza and yanaka cemetary near ueno park. A street of old stores and stuff u can find places to eat or buy and then u can walk towards a cemetary (lol) or to ueno park which has a zoo and the art museum iirc. u can then walk to akihabara and do stuff there
  • places2: ikebukuro. honestly theres tons of tourists here but i think more ppl craze over going to akihabara instead of ikebukuro when they virtually offer the same things

item.title: Hokkaido Ramen Santouka - Miso Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $20
  • Rating: 7/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-07-19
  • Review: a pretty classic bowl of miso. I’m not knowledgeable on hokkaido ramen and reading online I’m still clueless, so my view might be biased here. anyway, it was a decent bowl: noods, soup, bamboo shoots all good. I’d have preferred softer and juicer chashu, a more miso-centric soup (was slighlty weak), and maybe fresher woodear mushrooms (felt a bit bland). That being said, I think the quality of this for being in america is better than I expected (especially for a chain restaurant), and I overall enjoyed it. Definitely a great starter for anyone wanting to eat more traditional ramen.

item.title: Jigemon Champon - Spicy Miso
item.description:
• Price: ¥980
  • Rating: 6.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-28
  • Review: the first sip of the soup brings a very filling flavor of the rich spicy miso broth. unfortunately , this soup is really rich the more you eat, the more overwhelming it becomes. on top of that, the toppings are really standard flavor that one’d expect for a cheaper bowl of ramen.

item.title: Kaze no Jin - Iekei-style Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥1000
  • Rating: 7.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-24
  • Review: supposedly popular w/ some students who attend tokyo uni (japans #1 uni) and i can see the appeal - cheap and volumey. nothing particular stands out though, the toppings are the iekei style ones (bean sprouts cabbage onions which are great) and chashu (which was mediocre at best). For a broke college student who also needs the time for studying/part-time job, a quick and filling bowl for ¥1000 here is probably the best one can get.

item.title: Kikanbou - Karashibi Miso Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥1130
  • Rating: 8.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-08-13
  • Review: been here b4 but didn’t review last time, so here’s a review. this place is miso ramen but it’s spicy as shit. you can customize the heat level and numbness level; I’m weak so I did medium spice and low numbness but I think I could’ve gone higher. Along w/ that, it comes with a fatty piece of chashu and stir fried bean sprouts and chinese chives. Everything is done amazingly well, the thicker noodles help catch the strong soup and the whole bowl packs a punch. Not to mention the toppings are all top notch and also catch the strong soup. My only gripe is I’d need to order an additional bowl of rice to dump into all the soup goodness once I’m done with the noods. I’ll def try that next time.

item.title: Menya Hidamari - Shio Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥950
  • Rating: 8.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-25
  • Review: seafood based shio broth that was ultra clean along w/ a bright velvety oil that coats everything well. the saffron and yuzu toppings add a nice cut thru the oil, and the two types of chashu (fatty and lean) make for a nice overall balance in the dish. For shio ramen lovers, the rating would be higher, but even for someone like me who doesn’t like shio ramen that much, it was really good.

item.title: Menya Usagi - Tantan Zousui Set
item.description:
• Price: ¥1230
  • Rating: 8.75/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-01-18
  • Review: tantanmen (based off the chinese dish dandanmian) is (technically) a ramen that adds a sesame sauce to the bowl of soup, serving a more sauce-like experience rather than the conventional soup that one is used to. This bowl has stirfried minced meat along w/ the sichuan-inspired chili oil featuring ma (numbness) and la (spicyness). Just based off this complex melody of flavors, and a low hydration noodle that maintains its firmness and doesn’t get soggy, I’d give an 8 already. HOWEVER, I think the star is truly the sauce+soup, and what’s great about the zousui set is that the bowl comes with rice and an onsen tamago (kinda like a poached egg). Once you finish the noods, you can add the rice and eggs into the soup and mix together, creating a spicy concotion that fully captures the spice, numbness, and umami from the soup. For this shime (conclusion), I give an increased score.

item.title: Menya Yoshi - Special Shoyu Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥1400
  • Rating: 8.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-23
  • Review: staff are friendly for deaf/hearing-impaired people which is great since you don’t find many inclusive places like this in jpn. also, usually when one imagines ramen they’d think of loudass busy places (stereotypically terrible for first dates) but this was quiet and tranquil. I found each topping fascinatingly fresh and explosive in flavor, especially the chicken chashu. the soup is a flavorful and clean seafood-based shoyu. the star is the velvety and clean chicken oil they use that enhances everything. the main downside is the broth is slighlty too salty, so I had to reset my palate w/ water a few times. Adding yuzu koshou halfway thru the bowl was a great flavor change and absolutely remade how I viewed the bowl, usually I add white pepper but the guy next to me added yuzu koshou so I did too.

item.title: Naoji - Seabura Chuuka Soba
item.description:
• Price: ¥980
  • Rating: 8.25/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-01-15
  • Review: this is chuuka soba that has a topping of raw diced onions and pork back fat (seabura) pieces. you’d imagine it to be very filling and heavy, but because of the light broth and raw onions, it cuts thru the fat well, leading to a very strong impactful bowl without weighing you down. very nice, though I wasn’t a huge fan of how the other toppings (chashu + menma) were.

item.title: random extra bio
item.description:
here I write completely random stuff about me.

🎮 current (as of Nov 2026) hobby rotation

  • street fighter 6: the main game I play solo, though I have other games in rotation to play w friends. I’d like to get better at it, but I think I’ve underestimated how hard it is to get good and am thus hardstuck.
    • I’ve gotten so far: Ed, Ryu, Cammy, Ingrid, Jamie to master rank. I mainly now play Jamie and aim to climb up as high as possible with him.
    • controller: ArcadeShock traveller leverless case; thirteen 24mm Flashtaps + two 30mm Flashtaps (the blue buttons); three sanwa 24mm purely for option/ps/share button (the orange ones); brook gen 5 fighting board. This was my first time making a custom leverless and I struggled a lot with getting clean wire management. Nonetheless, I really like the entire setup - particularly the button layout since I like using my left thumb for jump and my right thumb for drive impact - and I’ll hope to use this for a long while.
  • boxing: go around twice a week, in addition to jogging once or twice a week. objective: fun, exercise, stress-release, challenge, etc.
  • read books; watch movies.

🦑 My thoughts on food

  • If I could, I’d be eating 24/7. I like food a lot and can talk about it for years.
  • My favorite food is the pho I find around Jackson Heights / Elmhurst. I get all the types of meat (I like tripe and tendon especially) and add all the bean sprouts, lime, and herbs. Depending on the day I may or may not add a bit of sriracha in the soup but not too much such that it covers the flavor of the broth.
  • I don’t avoid any particular foods though I don’t think I see myself eating mammals besides pigs, cows, goats/lambs/sheep. I did eat horse meat before as it’s a thing in Japan; it didn’t leave much of an impression so I don’t think I’ll try it ever again.
  • Oh, but I do think chocolate is overrated. Chocolate ice cream, cake, pain au chocolat, cocoa puffs. Literally none of them are even close to being my go-to-choice. I do like me a good chocolate truffle though.
  • Steak is also overrated. I do enjoy all of them: dry-aged, steak and eggs at 2 am in IHOP, picanha, wagyu, etc. But it’s just so pricey for what. Also surely not all high-end restaurants aren’t one trick ponies only able to serve expensive pieces of steak with a buttload of truffles and caviar right? I know a select are innovative (e.g. The French Laundry), but every YouTube video highlights steak, truffles, and caviar ONLY.
  • I currently have three knives: a gyuto, pairing, and nakiri. All three are Japanese handcrafted steel. The first two have a western grip and the last a Japanese wooden grip. Personally I find western grips favorable.
  • The best and laziest dish I’d recommend making is buldak-sauce fried rice:

Follow J Kenji Lopez Alt’s recipe in making fried rice in a home setting (without the blowtorch stuff) using whatever toppings you’d like. Instead of adding all the sauces at the end though, just add half a packet of the sauce that comes in the 1x spicy buldak ramen. Mix it around and serve.

item.title: Red White Boneless Ramen - Red Hot Miso Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $20
  • Rating: 6.5/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-06-29
  • Review: this is probs the second vegetarian ramen I’ve had. Flavor was not bad, and actually pretty decent. Unfortunately, it’s kinda one dimensional and not surprising. The toppings are interesting but not in a positive way. The fact that it’s vegetarian is nice, but overall there are ways to make it better without using tofu as a meat substitute. It’s kinda pathetic that people still use tofu as a meat substitute bc it’s really more than that. menma, woodear mushrooms, seaweed are more classic, add better texture, and would really suit a miso ramen. tofu is still fine here (given that tofu is often found in miso soup), but I didn’t enjoy the taste of the firm tofu (which is pretty common compared to sofu tofu). Idk why there’s a decent line for this place, 6.5/10.

item.title: Shichimencho - Ajitama Shoyu Ramen
item.description:
• Price: ¥970
  • Rating: 8/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-26
  • Review: textbook definition of classic shoyu ramen with a bit of tweaks: seafood broth, lean tender chashu, and straight up bamboo shoots instead of menma (this is great imo the star of the dish). Great bowl of ramen, classic flavors.

item.title: Shinshyuu - Tonkotsu Miso
item.description:
• Price: ¥1030
  • Rating: 6/10
  • Last date I had it : 2024-12-20
  • Review: individually, all the components work well but nothing particularly amazing. the chashu and egg are average, and what brings the bowl down is the broth thats too salty. perhaps this is just an unlucky batch w/ too much miso added, but overall it makes the ramen overbearing. also the alkali flavor is somehow pretty strong in the noods, maybe the strong soup is causing the noods to taste too strong.

item.title: WakuWaku Ramen - Signature Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $18
  • Rating: 6/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-05-30
  • Review: (First, I’ll preface that the ramen comes w a side of tonkatsu, but I’m only giving a review for the ramen) Why is there god damn corn? Anyway, now that that’s out of the way: I think this is pretty average or mediocre. The individual components are decent, but there’s a lot of improvements possible. The soup is kinda thin, both in terms of strength and saltiness. One can also consider the funkiness too weak as well, but that’s preference. The noods were probs too alkali-tasting and were overcooked, which I think is the opposite of what you want from tonkotsu style ramen. I think the scallion topping was nice and unique, and the bok choy is reasonable. The chili oil was also interesting but lacked punch. The bowl overall felt muted, and could have had additional brightness, either thru some more acid added from a topping or potentially as an extra flavor component to the chili oil. Else, don’t add the chili oil at all, and instead let the customer add if they want. I say this b/c the chili oil got repetitive real fast. Lastly, despite being the “signature” ramen, nothing felt unique nor stood out to be defined as an “identity.”

item.title: Yume wo Katare - Jiro-style Ramen
item.description:
• Price: $18
  • Rating: 8/10
  • Last date I had it : 2025-05-24
  • Review: my second time trying jiro, this time in cambridge. overall, a really balanced bowl, you ofc have everything you expect, super strong garlicky soup w/ tons of oil and flavor, the noodles and chashu had great texture, and overall very filling. Probably one of the best bowls of ramen I’ve had in America. My only gripe is that I couldn’t really customize the toppings: they just assume you want everything in a “moderate” amount. I definitely wanted a lighter soup w/ a shit ton more veggies as that style would help to take in this heavy monstrosity. that being said, this bowl was nonetheless solid, and the shop had an interesting atmosphere where customers can shout out their “dreams” if they finish their entire bowl (including the soup). I didn’t participate in that, I was just god damn hungry.
